title: Place value up to hundreds of thousands
description: What each digit is worth according to the place it occupies. The answer is written, not chosen: each question says which place the mistake was in, so only that one needs revising.

questions.text: In the number 4,573, how many tens are there in the underlined digit, the 7?
hints: The 7 is in the second place counting from the right
questions.explanation: The 7 occupies the tens place, so there are 7 tens, that is 70 units.

questions.text: What value does the 5 represent in the number 4,573?
hints: It is not worth 5, it is worth 5 of something bigger
questions.explanation: The 5 is in the hundreds, so it represents 500. The digit is 5 and its value is 500: two different questions.

questions.text: Write in digits: 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 units.
questions.explanation: 308. Without the zero it would read 38, which is another number: the zero holds the tens place.

questions.text: Break 6,204 into the sum of its place values, separated by the + sign.
hints: Start with the thousands and work down
questions.explanation: 6,204 = 6000 + 200 + 4. The tens do not appear because there are 0 tens.

grader.feedback: The number is right, but the question asked for the decomposition, not the total.

questions.text: Which digit occupies the thousands place in 172,605?
hints: Count four places from the right
questions.explanation: Counting from the right: 5 units, 0 tens, 6 hundreds and 2 thousands.

questions.text: What is the name of the place the 1 occupies in 172,605?
hints: It is the highest place in this number

questions.text: Put these in order from smallest to largest, separated by commas: 4507, 4057, 4570.
hints: Compare digit by digit starting from the left
questions.explanation: All three have 4 thousands, so the next digit decides: 0 < 5, and then 07 < 70. The order is 4057, 4507, 4570.

questions.text: If you take all the hundreds away from 3,480, what number is left?
hints: 3,480 has 4 hundreds, and each hundred is worth 100
One thousand is a thousand units

questions.text: Write the largest number you can with the digits 5, 0 and 9, using each one once.
hints: The largest digit has to occupy the highest place
questions.explanation: 950. The 9 goes in the hundreds because that is where it is worth most, and the 0 goes last because a number cannot start with it.
